## Project Description

This experiment examines how exposure to concentrations of microplastics relevant to end-of-century predictions affects the thermal tolerance (CTmax), acclimation capacity, and metabolic rate of Skistodiaptomus pallidus under ambient and elevated temperature conditions relevant to end-of-century heatwave predictions. The CTmax of four treatment groups will be compared at the end of a 7 day treatment period, with each group having either no MPs or MPs present and having either control temperatures (16C) or heatwave temperatures (22C). Results will improve our understanding of how multiple stressors interact to shape copepod resilience in a warming, plastic-polluted world.

## Questions, Objectives, Hypotheses

Questions:
1. How does exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs affect the thermal tolerance of S. pallidus?
2. Do MPs affect S. pallidus's ability to acclimate to end-of-century heatwave temperatures?
3. Does exposure to MPs affect the metabolic rate of S. pallidus?

Hypotheses: 
1. Exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs will cause an increase in thermal limits because of stress pathways activated by the MPs being similar to thermal resistance stress pathways.
2. MPs will increase S. pallidus's acclimation ability to end-of-century heatwave temperatures.
3. Exposure to MPs will increase the metabolic rate of S. pallidus to help cope with the stress.

## Study Design

This section should provide a detailed description of the study design. In addition to protocols and methodological details, this section should include a detailed accounting of replication and sample sizes.


Species: Skistodiaptomus pallidus #Species 
Generation: F>3
Temperature Treatments: 16C (Control), 22C (Warm)
MP Treatments: None, Present
Trait Measurement: CTmax
Population: *which population are we going to use: unknown*  
Replicates: 3
Animals/dish = 30 
Total animals needed = 90 (x/replicate)

1. Animals are collected from field and brought to lab.
2. On setup day X adult females are selected from the lab culture and are evenly split into four different dishes with XmL of DIO and ~0.5mL-1.5mL C. ozolini.
3. By the end of setup there will be four dishes: N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W, and each dish will have X animals.
Equation used to get # animals/dish: 
Animals/dish = ((# of assays * # of tubes)/# of dishes) + (0.5 * # of assays)
4. Dishes are given their respective amounts of MPs.
5. Each dish is placed into their respective incubators, a temperature sensor is also placed in the incubators in a dish with 150mL of tap water to closely monitor the internal temperatures of the incubators (in the incubator there are two shelves, the temperature treatments are always on the same shelf as one another but alternate every replicate, also the incubator that is used as the control or the warm alternates every replicate).
6. On day 7, 4 CTmax assays are ran using 2-3 animals from each dish in each assay. Tube placements for each assay are randomized using Skisto_LARA/Scripts/00_tube_assignments.R
7. This is replicated 3 times.

## Statistics

### Data Processing 

Data is processed in the controller script:
- Pop = "thermometer" is filtered out
- CTmax values < 34.5 are filtered out
- acc_hours is defined
- datetime is mutated to fit our date and time format

### Key Summary Statistics

| Summary Statistic    |  Calculated For Which Groups  |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| Mean +/- Standard Deviation | CTmax for each treatment: N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W|
| Coefficient of Variation | CTmax for each treatment + thermal tolerance, how it changes over the course of the experiment, how the mean of rate of acclimation is across treatments |

Hypothesis 1:
- Tests of assumptions:

- How model fit will be evaluated: 
Using the performance package in R

- Post-hoc tests: 
The CTmax of the no-MP and MP-present groups will be compared at each acclimation temperature. Support for this hypothesis would appear as consistently higher CTmax in MP-present animals.


- Caveats/Caution when interpreting results:
This design is limited to two stressors, other potentially interacting factors (e.g., food availability, oxygen levels, pollutants) are not accounted for and could influence thermal tolerance in ways this experiment cannot detect.

- Handling missing values:
Any missing values will not be included in final data.
